div.l: A Good man there was of relygyon
And was a poore person of a toun
But ryche he was of holy thoughte ⁊and werk
He was also a lernyd man ⁊and a clerk
That cristis gospellis truely wolde preche
His paryshons deuowtly wolde he teche
Benygne he was ⁊and wonder dylygent
And in aduersyte full pacyent
And suche he was prouyd ofte sythes
Full lothe were he to curse for his tythes
But rather wolde he yeue out of doute
Vnto his poore paryshons aboute
Of his offryng ⁊and also of his substaunce
He cowde in lytyll thynge haue suffysaunce
Wyde was his parisshe ⁊and houses ferre a sondre
But he let not for rayn ne for thondre
In syknesse ner in myscheyf to vysyte
The ferrest in his paryssh more ⁊and lyte
Vpon his fete ⁊and in his honde a staf
This noble ensample vnto his shepe he yaf
That fyrst he wrought ⁊and afterwarde taught
Out of the gospel the wordes he caught
And this fygure he ekyd therto
That yf golde ruste what sholde yren do
For a preest to be fowle in whom we truste
No wonder is a lewde man to ruste
And shame it is yf a preest take kepe
A slusty sheperde ⁊and a clene shepe
Well ought a preest ensample to gyue
By his clennesse how his shepe sholde lyne
Be sette not his benefyce to hyre
And lete his shepe acombre in the myre
And renne to london to saynt poulis
And seke hym a chauntrye for soulis
Other wyth a bretherhede to be wytholde
But dwelle at home ⁊and kepe his folde
So þᵗat the wulf ne may not it myscarye
He was a shepeherde ⁊and not a mercenarye
And though he holy were and vertuous
He was not to synfull men to dyspytous
